metric_units: balanced accuracy and macro F1 are proportions in [0,1] (multiply by 100 for percent); AUROC is dimensionless
scope: A clinical research comparison and three holds. Nothing here extends the eight-protocol matrix, the deployment topics or the 2026-09-22 evidence update, and no two results share a ranking.
medical_disclaimer: Research results on a public data set. Not a diagnosis, not diagnostic accuracy, and not a medical device or medical advice.

ds004584.question: can resting-state EEG separate a clinical group from controls, and how much of that is age and sex

cohort.composition: 100 people with Parkinson's disease and 49 controls, one site
cohort.selection: five stratified participant folds; every person is held out exactly once, and all of a person's windows stay together

models.label: Age and sex only
models.why_here: A confound comparator, not an EEG model. It shows what this cohort can be separated by without any brain signal, and it never enters a model ranking.

method.features: 60 named channels shared by four source layouts; first 120 seconds; 30 disjoint four-second windows; log relative power in five bands spanning 1-45 Hz
method.aggregation: 300 features averaged within each person, so the classifier sees one vector per person rather than 4,470 independent examples
method.classifier: training-fold-only StandardScaler and a fixed balanced logistic regression (C=1)
method.tuning: one split seed, no held-out tuning
method.interval_kind: descriptive stratified participant bootstrap, 2,000 resamples; descriptive because the cross-validation training folds overlap

ds004584.claim_boundary: Research case/control discrimination only. Not a diagnosis, not diagnostic accuracy, not independent-cohort replication, not cross-site generalisation, and not online BCI performance. No patient-facing interpretation is supported.

independent_audit.replayed: 149 recordings and 4470 spectral windows with a separate FFT, all classifiers refit

rights.privacyReview: Every participant gave written informed consent, and decisional capacity was established, in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki; all research protocols were approved by the University of Iowa Human Subjects Review Board (IRB 201707828). One site, the University of Iowa Movement Disorders Clinic. The recordings are released CC0 by the authors. This is a clinical population, so the publication boundary is tighter than elsewhere on this site: only two model-level scores with descriptive intervals are published. No participant rows, per-person predictions, clinical or cognitive scores, medication state, or per-group age and sex composition — the last of these is in the reviewed inputs and is deliberately left out, because this site does not publish demographic profiles of a diagnosis-specific group. Nothing published here is diagnostic, and no participant can be distinguished in it.

Padding, truncating to the shortest common length, or reporting a partial cohort under the frozen protocol were all refused. What is published is the status and the source-defect counts; no accuracy row exists to publish.

status_only.name: L-FAME · six-person expansion
status_only.reason: An audited relative-spectrum description exists for 60 recordings from 6 people, and it is not a model result. Its per-condition numbers are withheld: the descriptors are summarised over 12 recordings per condition from those 6 people, so a minimum or maximum is one person's recording, which this site does not publish. Electrode-row mapping and physical units also remain unresolved, so a spectral profile cannot be read as a biological finding. The published record is the status and the cohort size.
